newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MINISTER AMENDS BILL FOR S.AFRICAN REVENUE SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: MINISTER AMENDS BILL FOR S.AFRICAN REVENUE SERVICE.

text.p: Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Tuesday introduced a wide range of amendments aimed at fine-tuning the South African Revenue Services (SARS) Bill due to be debated in parliament on August 19.

The bill, which provides for a merger of the departments of inland revenue and customs and excise, allows for administrative autonomy of the new service from the public service but keeps it under the final control of the Finance Minister.

The bill has been criticised because it does not provide the SARS with enough autonomy, especially on the financial side. This is believed to have led to the surprise resignation earlier this year of then SARS chief executive Piet Liebenberg.
Manuel refused to comment on Liebenberg's resignation but said that he had found no examples internationally where revenue services were completely independent.
"No examples spring to mind," he told the parliamentary finance committee.

At the same time, he said the government had to take into consideration the skills levels available in South Africa, where many large corporations had reported they had not been assessed for several years because of weak tax collection systems.

He said it had been decided not to grant the SARS a certain percentage of tax collected to meet running costs, as originally decided, because this would leave it worse off than if it had its own budget allocated by parliament.

Parliament, and the finance committee in particular, will in future have an oversight role over SARS and will be able to influence it in that way but no provision is made to include MPs on the SARS board.
The board is planned to be as broadly representative as possible. Manuel said however it should not be so representative that it did not have people with the right kinds of skills to advise the SARS.
The board would advise on technical matters and not tax policy, he added.
The SARS would also have the right to buy or rent its own buildings rather than rely on the Department of Public Works and would be able to outsource information technology requirements.
Manuel said everything possible had been done to allay any staff fears about the effects of being transferred from the public service to the SARS.
